newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European nuclear industry criticises Swedish move.
newsitem.headline: European nuclear industry criticises Swedish move.

text.p: The Association of the European Nuclear Industry (FORATOM) said on Thursday it "was extremely disappointed" by the Swedish government's plan to close the privately-owned Barseback nuclear power plant.
FORATOM said that the decision was made solely for political reasons and that the two Barseback reactors at the southern tip of Sweden provided clean, competitively priced electricity.

"The decision to close the Barseback plant is obviously exclusively based on a political manoeuvre and has nothing to do with safety or concern about the environment," the Brussels-based organisation said in a statement.

"FORATOM finds it especially disturbing that a governing party would would take a decision which expropriates private property," it said, adding that it supported owner Sydkraft it its resistance to an imposed plant closure.
FORATOM said it would support as "fully justified" any claims by Sydkraft for full compensation for closure costs.
It said electricity in the initial phase must be imported to replace the power from the Barseback plant and that the only available exports were fossil-fueled electricity from Denmark and Germany.
"A decision to import power merely shifts the revenue to exporters while penalising the Swedish consumer -- it makes no rational sense from an ecologic or economic point of view," FORATOM said.

The Danish government has has been arguing for a closure of the Barseback plant, and if it were successful, this would set a "dangerous precedent which the European nuclear industry will fight with all means at its disposal."

Under an energy agreement approved by Sweden's ruling Social Democrats and two other political parties this week, the proposed closures of the two Barseback reactors would take place by July 1998 and July 2001.
